agents.name: Ceritinib
agents.explanation: Ceritinib inhibits ALK signalling in a tumour with a confirmed ALK rearrangement. It can affect healthy tissues too, so blood tests and symptom checks continue even when treatment is taken at home.
agents.watch: Report breathing changes, fainting, jaundice, severe abdominal pain, persistent diarrhoea/vomiting or marked thirst promptly.
risks: Heart rhythm changes and slow pulse
Poor appetite, fatigue and weight loss

teachback: Can you explain taking the prescribed dose with food, the 12-hour missed-dose instruction, what to do if you cannot eat, your next liver test and when to call urgently?
consent_support: Discuss the post-crizotinib setting, aim and uncertainty, alternatives including not proceeding, material risks, daily treatment and food burden, interactions, pregnancy/fertility/feeding, monitoring and your right to reconsider. This aid is not treatment authorisation.
urgent_extra: Contact oncology urgently for new or worsening cough or breathlessness, fainting, palpitations, severe dizziness, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, severe persistent abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, poor drinking or little urine, or marked thirst with frequent urination and feeling unwell. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or severe chest pain needs emergency help.
purpose: Ceritinib blocks abnormal ALK signals that help some lung cancers grow. In advanced cancer after crizotinib, the aim is to control cancer and delay progression. The choice depends on your tumour test, previous treatment, other options and priorities.

support.title: Prevent and treat nausea
support.text: Ceritinib has moderate-to-high oral sickness risk. Ask for daily prevention and rescue instructions. Your team must check heart-rhythm and medicine interactions when choosing anti-sickness treatment; do not add medicines or a steroid course yourself.

support.title: Food and daily doses
support.text: If illness prevents you eating with the dose, contact the team. Only the prescriber can arrange a different fasting dose. Do not alternate between fed and fasting schedules or change the dose yourself.

support.title: Check interactions
support.text: Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice and St John’s wort. Check prescription, pharmacy and herbal medicines before use, including heart medicines, antibiotics, antifungals, seizure treatments and acid-reducing medicines. Do not stop a prescribed medicine without advice.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and feeding
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding before treatment. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months afterwards; hormonal contraception may be less effective, so agree a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during this treatment. Fertility effects are uncertain; ask about preservation if relevant.

support.title: Diarrhoea, fluids and daily life
support.text: Use the agreed diarrhoea treatment promptly. Report persistent symptoms, poor intake or dehydration. Ask for help with appetite, fatigue and practical support; avoid driving or machinery if fatigue or visual symptoms affect safety.

evidence.title: Evidence after crizotinib and for dosing with food
evidence.intro: Study results describe groups, not an individual forecast.
evidence.population: Advanced ALK-positive NSCLC; post-crizotinib/platinum ASCEND-5 and separate dose-optimisation ASCEND-8 populations.
evidence.comparison_label: Historical chemotherapy or alternative food/dose schedules
evidence.interpretation: A study after crizotinib and platinum chemotherapy found longer disease control with ceritinib than the chemotherapy used at that time. It tested an older fasting dose. A separate dose study supports taking the current lower dose with food; its main efficacy group had not had previous treatment. These studies cannot predict your outcome or rank all current treatment options.
evidence.limitations: Trials used different doses and populations. No proven individual benefit or cross-trial ranking is implied.

chronology_notes.title: No planned rest week
chronology_notes.text: The usual starting dose is 450 mg once daily with food, every day without a planned rest week. Follow your own prescription. Treatment continues while it helps and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed course length.

chronology_notes.title: Early liver checks
chronology_notes.text: Liver tests every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then monthly; earlier if abnormal.

chronology_notes.title: If a dose is held
chronology_notes.text: The clinician confirms recovery and authorises any restart. Do not restart from this timeline alone.

port_pump.note: Oral ceritinib does not itself require an infusion line or pump.

administration_text: Take at the same time daily with food. Swallow capsules whole with water; do not chew or crush. Take a missed dose unless the next is due within 12 hours; ask your pharmacist if timing is unclear. Never double a dose. If you vomit, do not replace the dose; take the next at its usual time. If illness prevents you eating with the dose, contact the team. Only the prescriber can arrange a different fasting dose. Do not alternate between fed and fasting schedules or change the dose yourself.
monitoring_summary: Before starting: ALK test, blood count, kidney and liver tests, pancreatic enzymes, fasting glucose, ECG and symptom/medicine review. Blood count, kidneys and fasting glucose every 4 weeks; liver tests every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then monthly. ECG after 1 month, then as needed. Extra heart, electrolyte, glucose or pancreatic tests may be needed for risks, symptoms or abnormal results; scans follow the consultant plan.

items.title: Match evidence to your situation
items.text: ASCEND-5 involved previous crizotinib and platinum chemotherapy and an older fasting dose. ASCEND-8 supports the fed schedule but its main efficacy analysis was treatment-naive. Ask how these results fit your previous treatments and current alternatives.
